blocks.en: One of the most striking things about D'Alembert's solution (or more specifically, the form of the solution implied by \eqref{eq:wave-characteristic-split}) is that the formula for the solution makes perfectly good sense even when $f$ and $g$ are discontinuous. Such a "solution" would consist of a "jump" in $u$ moving to the left or right with unit speed. The existence of such solutions should not violate our intuition about the wave equation since physical wave-like phenomena that we would call discontinuous (such as breaking waves in the surf and shock waves from explosions) occur every day. But what about the mathematical nature of the solution? How can we say that a solution satisfies a differential equation at a point at which it is not differentiable? In later chapters we will examine this question more fully, and especially in the context of generalized wave equations we will get some fairly detailed answers.
blocks.zh: D'Alembert 解 (更具体地说, \eqref{eq:wave-characteristic-split} 所蕴含的解的形式) 最引人注目的特点之一是, 即使 $f$ 和 $g$ 不连续, 解的公式仍然完全有意义. 这样的"解"将包含 $u$ 中的一个以单位速度向左或向右移动的"跳跃". 这类解的存在不应违背我们对波动方程的直觉, 因为我们会称为不连续的物理波动现象 (例如近岸破碎波和爆炸产生的激波) 每天都在发生. 但解在数学上的性质如何? 在解不可微的点, 怎么能说它满足微分方程呢? 后面各章将更充分地研究这个问题, 尤其将在广义波动方程的背景下得到一些相当详细的答案.

blocks.en: In this section we derive a result for solutions of the wave equation known as conservation of energy. We prove a version here that holds for the one-dimensional wave equation with fixed ends defined above and leave generalizations for later chapters.
blocks.zh: 本节推导波动方程解的一个称为能量守恒的结果. 这里证明适用于上面定义的两端固定的一维波动方程的版本, 将推广留到后面各章.

blocks.en: Note that the quantity we call the energy for solutions of the wave equation and the quantity we call the energy for solutions of the heat equation seem very different mathematically. However, the mathematical techniques that we use to study the quantities (multiplication of the differential equation by the solution or its derivative and (essentially) integrating by parts in order to obtain an estimate) are common to both. This technique of obtaining estimates on solutions of PDEs is extremely useful and is generalized in later chapters.
blocks.zh: 注意, 我们称为波动方程解的能量的量, 与称为热方程解的能量的量, 在数学上看起来很不相同. 然而, 研究这两个量所用的数学技巧是共同的 (将微分方程乘以解或其导数, 再 (实质上) 分部积分以获得估计). 这种获得偏微分方程解的估计的技巧极为有用, 后面各章将加以推广.

blocks.en:
Solve the one-dimensional wave equation via separation of variables for the following boundary conditions:\begin{enumerate}[label=(\alph*)]
\item $\begin{aligned}u(x,0)&=x^2-x,\\u_t(x,0)&=0,\\u_x(0,t)&=0,\\u_x(1,t)&=0.\end{aligned}$
\item $\begin{aligned}u(x,0)&=0,\\u_t(x,0)&=\sin\pi x,\\u(0,t)&=0,\\u_x(1,t)&=0.\end{aligned}$
\end{enumerate}
blocks.zh:
用分离变量法求解满足下列边界条件的一维波动方程:\begin{enumerate}[label=(\alph*)]
\item $\begin{aligned}u(x,0)&=x^2-x,\\u_t(x,0)&=0,\\u_x(0,t)&=0,\\u_x(1,t)&=0.\end{aligned}$
\item $\begin{aligned}u(x,0)&=0,\\u_t(x,0)&=\sin\pi x,\\u(0,t)&=0,\\u_x(1,t)&=0.\end{aligned}$
\end{enumerate}
blocks.label: ex:wave-two-boundary-problems

source_locations.bbox_precision: visually selected parent block, top-left PDF points

blocks.en: Give a specific definition of well-posedness (in particular, make precise in what sense the problem is continuous with respect to the data) for the Cauchy problem \eqref{eq:wave-one-dimensional}, \eqref{eq:wave-cauchy-initial-position}, \eqref{eq:wave-cauchy-initial-velocity} on the domain $(x,t)\in(-\infty,\infty)\times(0,\infty)$. Derive conditions on the initial data under which the problem is well-posed. How do your results differ if the domain under consideration is $(x,t)\in(-\infty,\infty)\times(0,T)$ for some $0<T<\infty$. Hint: If $u(x,0)=0$ and $u_t(x,0)=\epsilon>0$ for $x\in(-\infty,\infty)$, then $u$ grows arbitrarily large with time. Figure out conditions on the initial data that assure that $u$ stays bounded.
blocks.zh: 对区域 $(x,t)\in(-\infty,\infty)\times(0,\infty)$ 上的 Cauchy 问题 \eqref{eq:wave-one-dimensional}, \eqref{eq:wave-cauchy-initial-position}, \eqref{eq:wave-cauchy-initial-velocity}, 给出适定性的具体定义 (特别要明确问题在什么意义下连续依赖于数据). 推导使问题适定的初始数据条件. 如果所考察的区域改为某个 $0<T<\infty$ 对应的 $(x,t)\in(-\infty,\infty)\times(0,T)$, 结果会有何不同. Hint: 如果对 $x\in(-\infty,\infty)$ 有 $u(x,0)=0$ 且 $u_t(x,0)=\epsilon>0$, 那么 $u$ 随时间增长会变得任意大. 找出保证 $u$ 保持有界的初始数据条件.
blocks.label: ex:wave-cauchy-wellposedness

source_locations.bbox_precision: visually selected parent block, top-left PDF points

blocks.en: Suppose $f$ and $g$ are identically zero outside the interval $[-1,1]$. In what region in $(-\infty,\infty)\times[0,\infty)$ can you ensure that the solution $u$ of the Cauchy problem is identically zero.
blocks.zh: 设 $f$ 和 $g$ 在区间 $[-1,1]$ 外恒为零. 在 $(-\infty,\infty)\times[0,\infty)$ 的什么区域内, 可以保证 Cauchy 问题的解 $u$ 恒为零.
blocks.label: ex:wave-finite-propagation-region

Is there a similar result to the previous problem for the heat equation? Hint: Use
\[
\chi_{[-1,1]}(x):=\begin{cases}1,&x\in[-1,1]\\0,&x\notin[-1,1]\end{cases}
\]
as initial datum. Use Problem~\ref{ex:heat-step-cauchy-problem} to obtain a solution.

对于热方程, 是否有与上一题类似的结果? Hint: 使用
\[
\chi_{[-1,1]}(x):=\begin{cases}1,&x\in[-1,1]\\0,&x\notin[-1,1]\end{cases}
\]
作为初始数据. 利用 Problem~\ref{ex:heat-step-cauchy-problem} 得到一个解.
